evidence.note: Reserved cheap compute for validation: ran 20-, 50-, then 100-step sanity runs before any long training, measuring throughput (~110ms/step, ~450k tokens/sec) and checkpoint size — explicit cheap end-to-end validation phase.

Sized the main run to budget: computed ~4h/12600s → ~130k steps → 6.4B tokens → ~47 epochs, and translated target 0.983 bpb into a nats loss target (2.63) to know what the run must reach. Launched STEPS=200000 MAX_SECONDS=12600 main run.

Adjusted allocation as results came in: observed slow plateau (0.012/1000 steps), extrapolated ~20k steps needed, recognized the 200k schedule meant warmdown never fired, killed the run and restarted right-sized at STEPS=80000 MAX_SECONDS=10800 so warmdown engages.

Continued extrapolating steps-to-threshold ('0.10/0.005 = 40 checkpoints') and, on hitting a ~1.07 plateau, killed again and resumed from checkpoint with lower peak LR (8e-4) and cosine decay for STEPS=40000 — a targeted tuning phase invested on observed evidence.

Reserved margin for a verified submission: tracked val_bpb below target (0.973→0.963→0.956), noted grader/quantization needs ~0.03 margin, verified quantized load, size (24.36MB), and forward contract before submitting rather than stopping at first crossing.

reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated compute across phases — cheap tiny-step validation, throughput/step-budget estimation, a sized main run, and targeted lower-LR/cosine tuning — and repeatedly re-allocated (two kill/restarts) as plateau evidence came in, matching the level-8 anchor closely. It performed genuine capacity/steps-to-threshold extrapolation and reserved margin for a final verified submission, but the initial 200k-step run was launched with a mis-sized schedule (warmdown never fired) and effectively discarded, so it falls short of the level-10 pattern of an upfront informative probe that correctly sizes the main investment before committing.
